title: Jazz and Modern Popular Music
summary: Jazz grew in New Orleans, a city whose large population of African descent kept West African and Caribbean traditions alive. By the 1890s brass bands there mixed ragtime into their march repertoire, and between 1895 and 1900 the cornetist Buddy Bolden began adding improvised blues and faster tempos to dance tunes, credited by early jazzmen as the first new style. On 26 February 1917 the first jazz record, Livery Stable Blues, was released, made, uneasily, by a white band, the Original Dixieland Jass Band, playing an African American genre.

uncertainty.note: Buddy Bolden and New Orleans brass and dance bands began incorporating improvised blues between 1895 and 1900, establishing the foundation of jazz music.
